document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify novel diagnostic plasma biomarkers for sport-related concussion (SRC) by investigating proteomic changes in collegiate athletes. It found 338 differentially abundant plasma proteins after SRC, with a combination of erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 (EPB41) and alpha-synuclein (SNCA) demonstrating high diagnostic accuracy, especially when measured more than 6 hours post-injury. The study also noted acute increases in cardiac-related proteins (troponin T, troponin I, and FABP3) post-SRC, suggesting physiological stress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnosis of Sport-related Concussion (SRC) using proteomic profiling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood samples were collected from concussed and non-concussed collegiate athletes within 48 hours post-injury, with analyses conducted for acute (0-6 hours) and subacute (7-48 hours) phases. A highly multiplexed proteomic DNA aptamers assay targeting 1305 plasma proteins was used. The study focused on biomarker discovery for diagnosis rather than a therapeutic intervention, thus no specific dose comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported, nor was a 'dose' of concussion administered or compared.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly more abundant after SRC (P<0.05). After 6 hours post-injury, individual plasma EPB41 showed an AUC of 0.956 (95%CI: 0.902–1.000); combination with SNCA provided an AUC of 1.000.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential erythrocyte membrane component, stabilizing the spectrin-actin cytoskeleton, and plays an essential role in the central nervous system.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sport-related concussion (SRC) diagnosis, particularly >6 hours post-injury.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A highly accurate plasma diagnostic biomarker for concussion in athletes, especially when combined with alpha-synuclein. Previously, decreased levels were associated with neurological impairments.
